description: How the AI behaviour a project builds is measured. A baseline, a candidate, a dataset, and a comparison between them. This is about the product; policies/evaluation-policy.json is about this organization's own agents, and the two are kept apart on purpose -- same discipline, different subject, and a suite that mixes them measures neither.

why_a_comparison.statement: A meaningful AI evaluation result is a difference against a baseline, not a number.
why_a_comparison.reason: An absolute figure answers almost nothing on its own. 87% correct is good or catastrophic depending entirely on what it was before, and the questions that decide a release are comparative: did the thing being fixed improve, did anything else get worse, and is the difference bigger than the noise between two runs of the same configuration.
why_a_comparison.consequence: A change with no baseline has nothing to compare against and cannot be assessed. Establishing the baseline is a stage of the workflow rather than a preparation for it.

the_four_versions.description: Every evaluation result names four versions, or it cannot be reproduced and cannot be compared with another.
the_four_versions.why: These four change independently and each changes behaviour. A result that names fewer is a number whose provenance is a guess, and two results that name different sets are not comparable at all.
the_four_versions.one_variable_rule: Baseline and candidate differ in at most one of the four. A prompt change and a model upgrade evaluated together produce a delta nobody can attribute, and the attribution is the entire value of the exercise.

artifacts.AIBC: The behaviour contract: what the system must do, stated precisely enough to be measured. Written before the change, not after.
artifacts.EVALSET: The evaluation dataset. Versioned, reviewed, in the repository.
artifacts.EVALRUN: One run of one configuration against one dataset. Baseline and candidate are both EVALRUNs; what distinguishes them is which one the other is compared against.

rules: Built from real inputs. Invented examples encode what the author expected, and what the author expected is not what is failing.

Includes the hard cases: ambiguous inputs, inputs whose correct answer is a refusal or a null, inputs that resemble a different category. A dataset of easy cases reports a high number and predicts nothing.
Every case carries an expected outcome somebody stands behind, and where that outcome is a judgement, whose.
Part of it is held out. A dataset the prompt was tuned against measures the tuning.
It is an artifact: versioned, reviewed, changed deliberately. A dataset edited to make a run pass is the same defect as a test edited to make a build pass, and it is harder to see.
dataset.growth: A defect found in production becomes a permanent case. That is the mechanism by which the dataset keeps describing reality rather than describing what the authors first imagined.

metrics.description: Dimensions a run may report. Report what the system's decision depends on; a metric nobody can act on is noise with a number.

correctness.means: The output was right for the input.

task_success.means: The end-to-end task completed, not just one call.

hallucination.means: The output asserted something not supported by its input or context. Measured as a rate, and it is the failure mode that looks most like success.

groundedness.means: The answer came from the provided context rather than from the model's own knowledge. An ungrounded correct answer is a wrong system that happens to be right today.

retrieval_quality.means: Was the right context available at all: recall at k, precision, and the rate at which nothing relevant was returned. Measured before answer quality, because almost every retrieval failure is debugged as a generation failure.

tool_call_correctness.means: Right tool, right arguments, right order.

refusal_behaviour.means: It refuses what it should and only what it should. Over-refusal is a failure and is usually unmeasured.

latency.means: Per call and per completed task, not per token.

cost.means: Per completed task. Tokens in, tokens out, calls per task.

robustness.means: Behaviour under paraphrase, typos, adversarial input and injected instructions.

regression.means: Not a dimension of its own: the change in any dimension against the baseline. Reported per dimension, because an improvement in the target and a loss elsewhere is the normal shape of a bad change.

metrics.evidence_rule: Every reported metric names the EVALRUN that produced it, and that run names its four versions and its dataset. A metric with no run behind it is not evidence, and reporting one is the failure this whole model exists to prevent.
never: Reporting a metric the run did not produce.
Reporting a metric from a different dataset version as though it were comparable.
Reporting an aggregate that hides a category that got worse.

deterministic.means: Exact match, schema validity, a rule, a retrieval hit, a tool-call comparison.
deterministic.properties: Cheap, reproducible, runs on every change.
deterministic.rule: Anything that can be deterministic is. A judged case where a rule would do is cost and variance bought for nothing.

model-judged.means: A rubric applied by a model where correctness is a judgement.
model-judged.properties: Real signal, and it carries a measurement error of its own: judges favour longer answers, favour their own outputs, and are affected by option order.
rules: Never auto-passed. Pending is a result; assumed is not.
Never the only gate on a safety-critical requirement. Back it with a deterministic case.
Validated against human labels on a sample before it is trusted.
Never judged by the model under test, on its own output.

modes.kept_apart: A run reports the two separately and never averages them into one figure. Merging them is how a suite stops meaning anything: the deterministic part stops being reproducible and the judged part stops being visible.

thresholds.shape: Gates on the comparison, not on the absolute.
thresholds.why: 'No dimension drops by more than x against baseline' survives a dataset getting harder; 'correctness above 90%' fails the moment the dataset starts including the cases that were always failing.
thresholds.noise: A delta smaller than the variation between two runs of the same configuration is not a result. Run the baseline twice before believing a small difference.
thresholds.regression_is_blocking: A regression in any dimension is a finding, including when the targeted dimension improved. Whether it is accepted is a human decision under the change's approval, not an averaging exercise.

enforcement.mechanism: artifact contracts and definition-of-done predicates on WF-AI-CHANGE
not_enforceable: Nothing verifies that a dataset is representative. A dataset of easy cases satisfies every predicate here and predicts nothing, and the only control is review by somebody who knows the domain.
Nothing verifies that a reported number was actually produced by the run it names. The predicate checks that the run exists and names its versions; it cannot re-execute it.
Nothing prevents a dataset being edited to make a run pass. It is an artifact under review like any other, and that is the whole of the control.
